ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #19
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What should you do before using a website for facts? (1 mark)
   A. Copy it without reading
   B. Believe everything
   C. Ask a teacher or parent and check the fact elsewhere
   D. Share your address

2. What is the plural of 'photo'? (1 mark)
   A. photoss
   B. photos
   C. photoes
   D. photees

3. Which sentence has correct capital letters and the correct ending? (1 mark)
   A. We went to Mombasa on Saturday,
   B. We went to Mombasa on Saturday.
   C. We went to Mombasa on Saturday?
   D. We went to mombasa on saturday

4. A sentence ends with (1 mark)
   A. a comma only
   B. a capital letter
   C. a colon
   D. a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark

5. Which question uses the pattern correctly? (1 mark)
   A. Do we enough have chairs to seat the guests?
   B. Enough chairs do we to seat the guests?
   C. Do we have enough chairs to seat the guests?
   D. Have we chairs enough to seat guests?

6. Which letter is a tall letter? (1 mark)
   A. h
   B. n
   C. e
   D. a

7. A caption is (1 mark)
   A. words that explain a picture
   B. a kind of camera
   C. a colour
   D. a song

8. What does 'thin' mean? (1 mark)
   A. very fat
   B. With little flesh on the body
   C. very tall
   D. very old

9. Which foods mainly give us energy? (1 mark)
   A. Salt and pepper
   B. Water and tea
   C. Ugali, rice and potatoes
   D. Vitamins only

10. When reading silently, you should (1 mark)
   A. read backwards
   B. sing
   C. read quietly in your head
   D. shout

11. A high, rising voice when we say 'Really?' shows (1 mark)
   A. anger only
   B. sleep
   C. surprise
   D. boredom

12. Which sentence usually ends with a falling voice? (1 mark)
   A. Is the file here?
   B. Did you send it?
   C. Where is the file?
   D. Can I use it?

13. Where do you see a reply to your email? (1 mark)
   A. In the keyboard
   B. On the wall
   C. In the inbox
   D. In the outbox

14. Which word has the /j/ sound although it begins with the letter u? (1 mark)
   A. uncle
   B. use
   C. under
   D. umbrella

15. Which of these tells you what a book is about before you read it? (1 mark)
   A. The printer's name
   B. The back cover summary
   C. The page numbers
   D. The price sticker

16. Choose the correct -ing form of 'make'. (1 mark)
   A. maiking
   B. makking
   C. making
   D. makeing

17. Which verb is NOT normally used in the progressive form? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. sing
   C. write
   D. know

18. Which sentence has the right capital letters and full stop? (1 mark)
   A. akinyi lives near river nzoia
   B. Akinyi lives near River Nzoia.
   C. akinyi lives near River Nzoia!
   D. Akinyi lives near river nzoia,

19. Which are pests? (1 mark)
   A. Tools for digging
   B. Small animals or insects that damage crops
   C. Tall trees
   D. Sacks for storing maize

20. When should you use a simile? (1 mark)
   A. Instead of full stops
   B. To help the reader picture something
   C. Only in questions
   D. Every second word

21. Which word in this sentence is the adverb? 'The nurse spoke gently.' (1 mark)
   A. The
   B. spoke
   C. nurse
   D. gently

22. What is the answer to this riddle? 'I am used to wash the body. I make bubbles and get smaller each time you use me.' (1 mark)
   A. a bucket
   B. a towel
   C. soap
   D. a broom

23. Which conjunction shows a result? 'The floor was dirty, ____ we mopped it.' (1 mark)
   A. yet
   B. so
   C. nor
   D. or

24. Which sentence uses the correct word? (1 mark)
   A. I no the answer.
   B. I know the answer.
   C. I nose the answer.
   D. I noe the answer.

25. Which word has the long vowel /ɔː/? (1 mark)
   A. cup
   B. door
   C. mud
   D. bus

26. Which word begins with the cluster 'sw'? (1 mark)
   A. green
   B. clean
   C. sweep
   D. broom

27. In which person is a diary usually written? (1 mark)
   A. Third person (he, she)
   B. No person
   C. Second person (you)
   D. First person (I, we)

28. What is a diary? (1 mark)
   A. A letter to a friend
   B. A newspaper
   C. A personal record of what happens to you each day
   D. A dictionary

29. Which sentence uses the correct preposition for a public vehicle? (1 mark)
   A. He is in the bus.
   B. He is at the bus inside.
   C. He is by the bus in.
   D. He is on the bus.

30. Which preposition completes: 'He borrowed money ____ his uncle.'? (1 mark)
   A. from
   B. by
   C. at
   D. of

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain the difference between 'good' and 'well'. Give one sentence for each. (4 marks)

32. Explain the difference between 'in' and 'into'. Give one sentence for each. (3 marks)

33. Explain how to use the five-finger test. (3 marks)

34. Put in order: Baraka presses Send; Achieng explains what an email is; they click Compose. (3 marks)

35. What kind of person is Baraka? Give one reason from the story. (3 marks)

36. Write two words that contain /ɛə/, two that begin with /j/ and one that has /ʒ/. (5 marks)

37. Write a sentence that has an adverb of manner, an adverb of time and an adverb of place. (3 marks)

38. Write three sentences about a car near a bridge using one subject pronoun, one object pronoun and one possessive pronoun. (3 marks)

39. Write four sentences for a short speech about your favourite game. (4 marks)

40. Give two reasons why we should read widely. (2 marks)

41. Fill in this form line with your own details in block letters: Name, Grade, School. (Write an example.) (3 marks)

42. Write one sentence with 'enough ... to' and one with 'a lot of' about your school. (3 marks)

43. Describe three things you do before, while and after reading a story. (3 marks)

44. Explain the difference between 'I have eaten' and 'I had eaten when he came.' (3 marks)

45. Put these events in order: (a) Omondi scored a goal. (b) Baraka spoke to Omondi. (c) The barber changed the blade. (3 marks)

46. Sort into countable and uncountable: rice, mango, time, book. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #19 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Ask a teacher or parent and check the fact elsewhere
   Checking a second source shows whether the fact is correct.

2. B — photos
   Photo just adds s.

3. B — We went to Mombasa on Saturday.
   Sentences start with a capital letter and names such as Mombasa and Saturday also need capitals.

4. D — a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark
   These are the marks that end sentences.

5. C — Do we have enough chairs to seat the guests?
   Enough comes before the noun chairs.

6. A — h
   H reaches the top line.

7. A — words that explain a picture
   Captions tell us what a picture shows.

8. B — With little flesh on the body
   Thin is the opposite of plump.

9. C — Ugali, rice and potatoes
   They are carbohydrates.

10. C — read quietly in your head
   Silent reading helps you focus.

11. C — surprise
   A rising voice can show surprise.

12. C — Where is the file?
   WH questions usually fall.

13. C — In the inbox
   Received messages are kept in the inbox.

14. B — use
   'Use' is said 'yooz', beginning with /j/.

15. B — The back cover summary
   The back cover gives a short summary.

16. C — making
   Verbs ending in silent e drop the e before -ing.

17. D — know
   'Know' describes a state, not an action in progress.

18. B — Akinyi lives near River Nzoia.
   Names and the first word begin with capitals, and the statement ends with a full stop.

19. B — Small animals or insects that damage crops
   Pests eat or damage crops.

20. B — To help the reader picture something
   A simile helps the reader imagine.

21. D — gently
   'Gently' tells how she spoke.

22. C — soap
   Soap makes bubbles and wears away.

23. B — so
   'So' shows result.

24. B — I know the answer.
   'Know' means to have learnt something.

25. B — door
   'Door' has /ɔː/; the others have the short /ʌ/.

26. C — sweep
   'Sweep' begins with s and w.

27. D — First person (I, we)
   A diary is about what I did and felt.

28. C — A personal record of what happens to you each day
   A diary records events and feelings.

29. D — He is on the bus.
   We say 'on the bus'.

30. A — from
   We borrow from someone.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: 'Good' is an adjective and describes a noun: She is a good singer. 'Well' is an adverb and describes a verb: She sings well.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule and 1 mark for each sentence.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: 'In' shows where something is: The coins are in the box. 'Into' shows movement to the inside: She put the coins into the box.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for examples.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Open a page and read. Hold up a finger for each new word. Count the fingers: few means the book is right, many means it is too hard.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the method, 1 mark for few, 1 mark for many.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Achieng explains what an email is; they click Compose; Baraka presses Send.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct position.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: He is kind and brave. He went to talk to Omondi, explained the facts and invited him to play.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a quality and 2 for the evidence.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: /ɛə/: chair, care. /j/: yellow, young. /ʒ/: television.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Yesterday the children played happily outside.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct adverb.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: It has bright head lights. The bridge protects us. The car is theirs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: A greeting, the name of the game, a reason, and a closing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: It builds vocabulary and improves reading speed and understanding. It gives knowledge and enjoyment.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Name: AMINA NJOROGE; Grade: 4; School: SUNRISE PRIMARY SCHOOL (any correct example).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each line in block letters.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: We have enough desks to seat every learner. The school has a lot of trees.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each pattern and 1 mark for correct punctuation.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Before: read the title and predict. While: read slowly and find meanings of new words. After: answer questions and retell.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each stage.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: 'I have eaten' says the eating is finished and it matters now. 'I had eaten when he came' says I finished eating before he came, in the past.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for the time link.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: (c), (b), (a)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct position.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Countable: mango, book. Uncountable: rice, time.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group.
